sections.h2: Ways to sell a house in Deptford
sections.html:
A Deptford owner can list with an agent, sell privately, or take an offer from a cash buyer. Condition and timing usually make the choice. A tidy house with months to spare suits the open market, while worn systems, tenants, an estate, or a payoff date on the horizon point toward a direct sale.

What slows a Deptford sale is rarely the buyer. It is usually an open permit, a repair nobody finished, or a form missing at the table. The sections below follow the township offices, then the Gloucester County Clerk, then the state forms attached to every deed.

  • Agent listing: the most exposure, with showings and a buyer who typically needs a mortgage and an appraisal.
  • Private sale: no commission to pay, though pricing, disclosures and the attorney review fall to you.
  • Cash purchase: no showings and no repair list, and the offer reflects the work the buyer inherits.

Deptford is a southeastern suburb of Philadelphia, about 10 miles from the city on the New Jersey side of the Walt Whitman Bridge. An estimated 32,600 people live in the township, up from 31,977 at the 2020 count. Most of the housing came with the post-war boom, when the population went from about 7,300 in 1950 to more than 24,000 by 1970. That age is why roofs, heating systems and wiring draw attention at inspection.

sections.h2: Location, schools and what buyers ask about
sections.html:
Access to Philadelphia is a selling point. Routes 41, 42, 45, 47 and 55 cross the township, and the New Jersey Turnpike is reached at Exit 3 in Bellmawr and Runnemede. NJ Transit buses on the 400, 401, 402, 408, 410 and 412 lines run to Philadelphia. Deptford Mall anchors the retail side, and Tall Pines State Preserve, a 111-acre park, sits on the border with Mantua Township.

One district, Deptford Township Schools, covers the whole township. The elementary schools are Good Intent, Lake Tract, Oak Valley and Shady Lane, Monongahela Middle School takes grades 6 to 8, and Deptford Township High School takes grades 9 to 12. Ask the district which elementary school your street feeds and give that answer to buyers early. Buyers also search by neighborhood name, including Oak Valley, Almonesson, Good Intent, Lake Tract, Jericho and Hammond Heights.

sections.h2: Does the 2021 tornado still matter when I sell?
sections.html:
It can. An EF3 tornado with winds up to 150 miles per hour, produced by the remnants of Hurricane Ida, struck Deptford on September 1, 2021 and damaged more than 100 homes. A repaired house should have closed permits and final inspections on file. A house patched without permits, or left half-fixed, can stall a mortgage buyer at inspection or appraisal.

If your house had storm repairs, collect the permit numbers, contractor invoices and insurance papers before you list. The township construction office at 1011 Cooper Street answers questions about open permits and final inspections at (856) 845-5300, weekdays from 8:30 until 4:30. A cash buyer can take unfinished work as it stands, and the offer will account for it.

The township construction office takes applications for a Housing Certificate of Occupancy. Before signing a contract, ask that office whether your sale needs one and what the inspection covers, since the buyer's attorney is likely to raise it.

Landlords have one more item. The township clerk's page cites N.J.S.A. 46:8-28, which requires rental owners to register with the clerk, and warns of fines reaching $500 for owners who skip it. If the house is tenant-occupied, make sure your registration is current. The Clerk's Office number is 856-686-2203.

sections.h2: What closing costs a Deptford seller
sections.html:
New Jersey puts the realty transfer fee on the seller. It is figured on a sliding scale for each $500 of price, and homes selling above $350,000 fall under a higher schedule. Your attorney or title agent can give you the exact number for your price before you sign.

  • Transfer fee: due from you at filing. If you claim an exemption, an affidavit (form RTF-1) goes in with it.
  • Recording: the Gloucester County Clerk adds a $20 indexing fee when a paper deed shows up without its cover sheet.
  • Seller's tax form: a GIT/REP form is signed at the closing table. Residents of New Jersey sign the GIT/REP-3 residency certification, while a seller living out of state may have to prepay at least 2 percent of the price.
  • Payoffs: whatever is owed on a mortgage, lien or municipal charge is taken out of what you receive.

Commission, if you list, is whatever your agreement says. Get that number in writing before you weigh a listing against a cash offer, because the two are only comparable on what you actually walk away with.

sections.h2: Where the deed goes after closing
sections.html:
Deptford deeds are filed with the Gloucester County Clerk. One of the GIT/REP forms must accompany every deed, and the Record Room answers at 856-853-3230. The county also runs a free Property Fraud Alert that notifies you whenever a document is filed under your name, which is worth setting up after a sale or an inheritance.

For a copy of an older deed, use the clerk's online land records search, where one can be printed free. Skip mailers that charge $75 to $86 for the same document.

sections.h2: When a direct sale is the better fit
sections.html:
A direct purchase fits when speed or condition matters more than the final few thousand dollars. In Deptford that might be a parent's house nobody wants to repair, a rental whose tenants are leaving, a property with storm or age damage, or a mortgage slipping behind. Get offers in writing, ask which closing costs the buyer covers, and set the net figure beside your best listing estimate.

Whichever route you pick, the order of work is similar. Call the construction office about the Housing Certificate of Occupancy and any open permits. Confirm your landlord registration if you rent the house out. Ask your lender and the township for payoff figures. Then hand your attorney the paperwork early, so the deed and the seller's tax form are ready when everyone sits down. If you are selling an inherited house, add the estate papers to that pile and ask the attorney who needs to sign.

faqs.q: Will a Deptford buyer take a house that needs work?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer takes the property as it stands and prices the work into the offer. A buyer relying on a mortgage may ask for repairs after the inspection or appraisal.

faqs.q: Which office files the deed for a Deptford sale?
faqs.a: The Gloucester County Clerk. The deed has to carry a GIT/REP form, and a paper filing without a cover sheet adds a $20 indexing fee. The Record Room number is 856-853-3230.

faqs.q: What transfer fee would a Deptford seller owe?
faqs.a: It grows with the price, per $500, and sales above $350,000 use a higher schedule. The seller pays it, so ask your attorney for the figure at your price.

faqs.q: Is there a township inspection before a Deptford sale?
faqs.a: Call the construction office at (856) 845-5300. It handles Housing Certificate of Occupancy applications and can say whether your sale needs one and what gets checked.

faqs.q: Does a rented Deptford house need landlord registration before I sell?
faqs.a: Rental owners register with the township clerk under N.J.S.A. 46:8-28, and the clerk lists fines reaching $500 for skipping it. Make sure yours is current before the buyer's attorney asks.
